title: Finance & Legal: Integrated Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, RevRec and Billing Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Purpose and scope

This playbook centralizes Redwood Inference's operating procedures for budgeting & forecasting, procurement, contracts lifecycle management, and revenue recognition (RevRec) & billing. It is intended for finance, legal, procurement, and partnering engineering/product teams who participate in budget planning, vendor selection, contract execution, and customer billing.

Sections included: budgeting & forecasting cadence, approval tiers and authorizations, procurement request-to-pay flow, contract intake and review checklist, RevRec policy summary and common billing scenarios, and escalation/runbook items.

1) Budgeting & forecasting (quarterly + annual)

Overview
- Goal: provide predictable financial planning to support product investments (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), capacity commitments, and go-to-market expansion while ensuring compliance with accounting policies.
- Timeframes: annual operating budget (AOB) cycle in Q4; rolling quarterly reforecast (RFR) every quarter; monthly variance review (MVR).

Owners and roles
- Budget owner: Product / Functional VP (e.g., VP Product) - owns top-line and spend target for the group.
- Budget coordinator: Finance Business Partner (FBP) - compiles inputs, produces consolidated model.
- Approving authority: CFO or delegated controller based on approval thresholds.

Inputs and models
- Revenue drivers: API usage growth, Dedicated reserved seats, Private deployment contracts, professional services run rate.
- Cost drivers: GPU spend (cloud + Dedicated pool), personnel, third-party SaaS, sales commissions, support.
- Modeling artifacts: ARR/MRR waterfall, headcount plan, unit economics for token costs per product route.

Cadence and deliverables
1. Annual planning (Q3-Q4)
   1) Finance publishes planning templates and baseline assumptions on Oct 1.
   2) Teams submit preliminary budgets by Nov 1.
   3) Finance consolidates and runs scenario analysis; leadership reviews Nov-Dec.
   4) Final AOB approved by CFO and CEO by Dec 31.
2. Quarterly reforecast (Q1-Q4)
   1) Rolling forecast template released 3 weeks before quarter-end.
   2) Teams submit updated forecasts 7 days prior to month-end close.
   3) Finance publishes consolidated forecast and variance analysis within 10 business days.
3. Monthly variance review
   - Owners must prepare a short deck explaining >10% variances to plan at owners' weekly review.

Approval thresholds
| Amount (USD) | Approval required | Approver backup |
|---------------|------------------|-----------------|
| up to 25,000  | Budget owner      | Finance BP      |
| 25,001 - 250,000 | Department head + Finance BP | VP Finance |
| 250,001 - 1,000,000 | CFO approval required | CEO notification |
| >1,000,000    | Board-level approval | CFO and CEO    |

2) Procurement: request-to-pay flow

Purpose
- Ensure standardized vendor selection, cost control, contracting hygiene, and audit trail for purchases of cloud, hardware, software, and services.

Procurement steps (request-to-pay)
1. Request initiation
   - Requester opens a Purchase Request (PR) in the procurement system with business justification, budget code, estimated total cost, and required delivery date. Attach vendor quote where available.
2. Budget validation
   - Finance BP validates available budget and attaches budget chargeback code. If funds are insufficient, the PR is escalated to the budget owner for reprioritization.
3. Sourcing & vendor selection
   - For spend > $50k: obtain at least 2 competitive quotes and conduct vendor risk check (security/compliance questionnaire).
   - For strategic vendors (platform, core infra): engage legal for preferred terms.
4. Purchase order (PO) and approval
   - PO is created by procurement after approvals per thresholds (see table above) and sent to vendor.
5. Receipt & invoice processing
   - Requester or receiving team confirms delivery. AP processes vendor invoice against PO with 30 net payment terms unless negotiated otherwise.
6. Vendor onboarding and payment
   - Procurement creates vendor record with W-9/FOB/TIN details and sets up payment terms in ERP.

Procurement controls and exceptions
- Emergency purchases: documented justification and retroactive approval within 5 business days.
- Single-source purchases require procurement and legal approval with documented reason.
- Capital vs expense treatment: finance classifies purchases based on capitalization policy (see related page: capital-expenditure-policy).

3) Contracts and legal process (lifecycle)

Objective
- Standardize contract intake, review, approval, execution, and storage to reduce legal risk and accelerate customer & vendor onboarding.

Contract intake checklist (required for every contract)
- Counterparty legal name and address
- Contract type (MSA, SOW, Subcontractor, Vendor)
- Term and renewal model (auto-renewal flags)
- Financial terms (pricing, billing cadence, termination liabilities)
- Data handling requirements (PII, PHI, residency) and required security attestations (SOC2, ISO27001, PCI if applicable)
- Confidentiality & IP clauses
- Insurance requirements and limits
- Special terms: export controls, sanctions, and audit rights

Review & approval flow
1. Intake via contract request form (legal intake)
2. Preliminary review by Legal (T+2 business days for standard templates)
3. Commercial review by Sales/Product (pricing & SOW)
4. Security & Privacy review for customer data needs or Private deployments
5. Final sign-off: Legal + Finance for revenue-impacting contracts; Procurement for vendor agreements.
6. Signing: use approved e-signature provider (DocuSign). Contract metadata is recorded in Contract Repository (link to repository).

Standard clause guidance and playbook references
- Use Redwood standard MSA template for Hosted API customers where possible. Deviations require Legal approval and change log.
- For Dedicated/Private deals, include SLAs (SLA uptime target 99.9% for Dedicated; contractual latency SLOs defined per tier) and data residency provisions.

Contract storage and audit
- All fully executed contracts must be uploaded to the central Contract Repository within 3 business days with metadata: contract id, counterparty, owner, effective/expiry dates, renewal notice windows, and financial terms.

4) Revenue recognition (RevRec) & billing policies (summary)

High-level principles
- Redwood follows ASC 606-style principles: identify contract(s) with customer, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, and recognize revenue when performance obligations are satisfied.
- Billing cadence and RevRec differ by product: Hosted API (usage-based), Dedicated (subscription/reserved capacity), Private (license + services), Professional services (time & materials or milestone-based).

Common scenarios and accounting treatment
- Hosted API (usage-based)
  - Transaction price: billed monthly in arrears based on metered usage.
  - Recognition: revenue recognized in the period usage occurred.
  - Deferred revenue: none for pure pay-as-you-go, except prepayments/credits.
- Dedicated (committed capacity)
  - Transaction price: subscription with contractual term and periodic billing (monthly/quarterly).
  - Recognition: recognized ratably over the contract term unless multiple performance obligations exist.
  - Upfront committed discounts: allocated across term and recognized over term.
- Private deployment & professional services
  - License fee: recognized over time or at a point in time depending on transfer of control and contractual terms.
  - Professional services: recognized based on completion of milestones or percentage-of-completion for multi-month engagements.
- Bundled arrangements
  - Allocate transaction price to distinct performance obligations using standalone selling prices; maintain RevRec allocation schedule.

Billing & collections playbook
- Invoice generation
  - Invoices generated by Billing system; standard terms net 30 unless negotiated. For enterprise deals, payment and milestone schedule captured in SOW.
- Dispute handling
  - Customer dispute lifecycle: customer raises dispute -> Billing triage within 3 business days -> if valid, credit memo/adjustment issued; if invalid, collections engagement starts.
- Collections and aged receivables
  - AR aging reviewed weekly; >60 days flagged to Finance + Sales for collections outreach. Legal escalation required for >120 days with material balances.

Journal entries (examples)
- Monthly Hosted API usage recognition (simple):
  - Dr Accounts Receivable
  - Cr Revenue (for usage recognized in month)
- Prepaid enterprise annual contract collected upfront:
  - On receipt: Dr Cash, Cr Deferred Revenue
  - As term elapses: Dr Deferred Revenue, Cr Revenue

5) Key controls, KPIs, and reporting

Controls
- Segregation of duties: procurement approvals separate from invoice approver and payment authorizer.
- Contract changes: material amendments >$250k must pass Legal + Finance + CEO approval.
- Audit log: all approvals captured in procurement and contract systems with user id and timestamp.

KPIs and reporting cadence
- Monthly close reports: MRR/ARR movements, revenue recognized vs billed, deferred revenue balance, DSO (days sales outstanding), and major contract renewals in next 90/180 days.
- Procurement metrics: PO cycle time, percentage of POs with competitive quotes (>50k), vendor risk scores.

6) Escalation and exceptions

Escalation path
- Level 1: Finance BP / Procurement manager (operational questions).
- Level 2: Head of Finance / Legal partner (policy disputes, contract deviations).
- Level 3: CFO / General Counsel (material exceptions, >$1M or high legal risk).

Emergency exception process
1. Submit emergency procurement form within 24 hours.
2. Obtain retroactive approvals from Budget owner and CFO within 5 business days.
3. Post-facto contract and compliance review by Legal.

Appendices and templates
- Attachments in the contract repository and procurement system: standard MSA, SOW template, procurement request form, vendor security questionnaire, capital vs expense decision tree, and revenue allocation worksheet.
- Sample vendor scoring rubric: 40% security, 30% cost/terms, 20% delivery capability, 10% strategic fit.

Related pages and references
- revenue-recognition-billing-policy-2026.json (detailed RevRec policy and ASC 606 guidance)
- finance-legal-budgeting-procurement-revrec-operational-guide-2026.json (operational templates and ERP instructions)
- contracts-procurement-playbook-2026.json (vendor onboarding and PO workflow)

Owner and review cadence
- Document owner: Head of Finance (Aisha Patel, Finance)
- Review cycle: annual review in Q4 or earlier if material policy change occurs.

Contact and feedback
- For questions about this playbook contact finance-ops@redwood-inference.internal or legal-intake@redwood-inference.internal.
